text:
alex: seeing a sudden latency spike across na-edge serving pools, started ~09:07 UTC. p50 up 4x, p95 > 1.2s. errors are "kvcache read timeout" and increased batch queueing. Noting a lot of spot GPU reclaims in the pool. @oncallbot — paging in case we need escalation
priya: Grafana – overlayed hotpool occupancy and batch queue length. hotpool at 98% and continuous-batcher queue depth spiking. Cloud shows mass preemptible evictions (GCP spot). bbox: https://grafana/redwood/d/edge/na-edge
jamie: any recent runtime deploys? I see a roll of continuous-batcher change 11m ago (commit a1b2c3) that changed max_batching_wait_ms from 8->12 and introduced a small kvcache refactor. Could be amplifying queueing when GPUs are scarce.
emily: network team reported transient egress congestion in na1 this morning — some BGP flap causing traffic to shift between zones. That plus spot reclaim would explain resource pressure + queueing.
alex: ops summary: (1) spot reclaim reduced available GPUs by ~30% in na-edge hotpool, (2) BGP egress jitter increased RPC latency, (3) continuous-batcher waits longer so more requests accumulate and hit KV read hot paths -> timeouts.
devops-bot: [autoscaler] downscale event detected: na-edge-hotpool-asg scaled in 6 -> 4 at 09:05 UTC due to cloud API transient. Suggested nodes: 2 reclaim events within 60s.
priya: mitigation checklist: 1) disable continuous-batcher temporarily for na-edge 2) increase hotpool target (if cloud has capacity) 3) route ~20% of traffic to na2 region 4) rollback kvcache refactor if latency persists
jamie: agree to disable batching first to stop queue amplification. I'll patch runtime config to max_batch_size=1 and set batching.enabled=false for na-edge. Rolling config id: cfg-1973
emily: I'll open a route-shift on the edge router to divert 20% to na2; keep healthchecks strict. Doing an incremental shift to avoid overload on na2.
alex: running commands now to set config: ```
# set batching disabled for na-edge
curl -X POST "https://console.internal/configs/apply" -d '{"env":"na-edge","runtime":{"continuous_batching":false,"max_batch_size":1}}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
```
alex: also scaling hotpool up while we confirm cloud capacity. kubectl/infra command: ```
kubectl scale deployment na-edge-hotpool --replicas=6 -n infra
```
devops-bot: [action] Scale request submitted to cloud provider: hotpool desired=6. Pending provisioning. Estimated time ~5-7m.
oncallbot: Incident created: INC-1973. Severity: high. Notify: eng-oncall, eng-runtime, networking. Runbook: "hotpool_capacity_squeeze_v1"
priya: after disabling batching we should monitor p95 and kvcache error rate. If KV reads still time out, enable kvcache fallback to read-only mode (serve stale from prefix-cache) — that will increase correctness risk but avoid tail latency.
jamie: preparing rollback patch for commit a1b2c3 in case config changes don't help. Patch PR #3420 queued, ready to merge.
emily: route shift 10% -> na2 now, will proceed to 20% in 2m if na2 health stable.
alex: observing initial signs of recovery: queue depth dropping, p50 trending down. Hotpool pods are Pending (cloud provisioning). kvcache read timeouts dropping but still present on a small fraction.
devops-bot: [cloud] 2 new GPU nodes provisioned and joined hotpool at 09:13 UTC.
priya: rolling extra safeguard: reduce max_batching_wait_ms to 4ms cluster-wide for now to minimize aggregation risk if batching comes back.
alex: updating runbook notes: actions taken: disabled continuous-batcher for na-edge; scaled hotpool -> 6; diverted 20% to na2; reduced max_batching_wait_ms; PR #3420 rollback ready; enabled incident channel.
emily: network team says BGP flaps resolved at ISP edge ~09:15 UTC, egress latency normalizing.
jamie: merging rollback if kvcache timeouts resurge after hotpool stabilizes. Otherwise will keep the refactor in canary until we can test more.
alex: endpoint metrics look much better: p95 down to 260ms, kvcache timeout rate <0.1%. Will keep this incident open 1 hour for monitoring. :thumbsup:
priya: cost note — scaling hotpool and diverting to na2 increases short-term spend. We'll open a cost ticket to reconcile. Tagging finance: @costs
